absent: Underlying raw read and write release mechanics and dependency release semantics.
Realtime base acquisition, release, trylock, nested, and contention internals.
Blocking semaphore and sleepable semaphore acquisition, release, waiter queuing, and wakeup behavior.
Sequence-counter writer increment protocol and full retry validation rules.
Interrupt, preemption, bottom-half, sanitizer, and assertion internals referenced as stubs.
Nestable write acquisition path validating a nest guard dependency map.

findings.text: SMP reader-writer primitive offers separate release operations for shared ownership and for exclusive ownership, each available in interrupt-restoring as well as interrupt-enabling as well as bottom-half-enabling shapes.

SMP release preserves dependency tracking release and raw ownership release before execution-context restoration, with interrupt shapes restoring preemptibility after interrupt handling and bottom-half shapes completing through bottom-half handling.
Realtime reader-writer interface exposes shared acquisition and shared release together with bottom-half guarded and interrupt flavored and flag-preserving variants plus a nonblocking shared attempt.

Realtime exclusive side exposes acquisition and release with subclass-aware and bottom-half guarded and interrupt flavored and flag-preserving forms, plus blocking and nonblocking attempts and a contention query.

Realtime interrupt flavored operations keep the historical flag parameter for compatibility but do not mask interrupts; preserving forms store a neutral value and plain forms leave interrupt state untouched while still performing the realtime ownership change.
Realtime bottom-half guarded operations bracket the underlying realtime ownership change with bottom-half suppression on entry and bottom-half restoration on exit.
Realtime contention query unconditionally reports absence of contention without inspecting lock state.

Traditional reader-writer lock object is built around an architecture raw component, with optional debugging ownership information and optional dependency tracking member present only under the corresponding configurations.
Realtime reader-writer lock object is built around a realtime base plus a readers count, with optional dependency tracking member present only when that tracking is enabled.
Reader-writer lock debug signature has value 0xdeaf1eed.

Statically declared reader-writer locks begin architecturally unlocked with debug ownership marked absent and dependency identity derived from the declaration name; realtime declarations instead begin from a realtime base initializer.

Sleepable semaphore in traditional configuration combines a count field with an owner hint and an optional spinner queue and a raw wait guard protecting the waiter head, alongside optional debug identity and dependency tracking.
Sleepable semaphore in realtime configuration contains only a realtime base and optionally a dependency tracking member.
Semaphore unlocked count value is zero while exclusive-held indication uses the lowest count bit.
Static semaphore starts with cleared count and cleared owner, unlocked wait guard, empty waiter head, and defaulted optional spinner plus debug plus dependency state derived from its name.

Semaphore exposes locked and contended predicates and held and write-held assertions; traditional forms inspect the count directly while realtime forms delegate to realtime base queries, and checked assertions select dependency-aware validation when available.
Semaphore waiter head is guarded by the internal wait guard; the contended predicate intentionally samples it without synchronization and therefore yields only a hint.
Header supplies scoped-guard constructors covering shared, tried shared, interruptible shared, exclusive, tried exclusive, killed exclusive, and initialization guard flavors.
Without nesting support, subclass-aware and nest-lock and killable-nested and non-owner aliases collapse to the plain shared or exclusive operations and discard the extra subclass or nest argument.

Dynamic initializers for reader-writer locks and sleepable semaphores and sequence counters allocate a per-site classification key and forward the textual name plus key to the low-level base initializer.
Counting semaphore combines an internal raw guard with an unsigned quantity and a waiter head, extended by a holder record only under hung-task blocker tracking.
Semaphore supports static declaration with a chosen initial quantity and dynamic setup that rebuilds the object around a new quantity and initializes dependency state for its internal guard.
Sequence-lock sanitizer region size bound is one thousand.

Sequence counter initialization establishes a zero numeric value with cleared dependency identity; the static zero form and the guardian-binding helper preserve that cleared start while optionally attaching a guardian pointer.

Sequence counter family includes a standalone form and guardian-bound forms for raw spin guard and spin guard and reader-writer guard and mutex guard styles, with generic accessors selecting behavior by operand type and zero initializers pairing a name with its guardian.

Counter read begins by acquiring an even snapshot, waiting while the value is odd, then exposing that snapshot for a later retry validation; unchecked and raw openings skip dependency marking and stabilization respectively while the checked opening adds reader dependency handling.

Guardian-bound snapshot acquisition on realtime preemptible configurations briefly cycles the guardian when an odd value is seen and then reloads; preemptibility reporting is suppressed on that configuration because the cycle provides progress.
Writer assertion for standalone counters demands disabled preemption, whereas guardian-bound counters demand that the associated guardian be held.
Sampling waiter presence without the wait guard can observe a transient queue state and must be treated as advisory rather than authoritative.
Read opening loops until the writer leaves the odd state, so an excessively delayed writer stalls readers; bounded sanitizer regions limit the associated analysis window.
